name: pdk-growthbook-sdk-payload-cache-no-stale-fill
instr:
We need SDK payloads to stay current across multiple GrowthBook back-end instances when customers publish flag changes. Extend the SDK payload cache for one organization, its `production` environment, feature revisions, and SDK connections without changing the existing publish and SDK routes.

For `SDK_PAYLOAD_CACHE=mongo`, every `/api/features/:key` response carries a numeric `revision` representing the committed feature value used to build it. After a successful `POST /api/v2/features/:id/revisions/:version/publish`, SDK reads from either instance reflect the published default value within `SDK_PAYLOAD_MAX_STALENESS_SECONDS` (3 seconds here). Cached payloads never move backward: a miss that reads before a publish but writes after a refresh cannot replace the newer cache, nor can a slower refresh from an earlier publish. Publishing may return before the refresh finishes; killing that instance immediately after its response cannot strand the change. Another running instance reconciles it within 6 seconds of the response.

For a registered SDK webhook, send changes only after the SDK cache holds the corresponding revision, at most once per revision, in revision order. Keep `SDK_PAYLOAD_CACHE=none` generating the current feature value without storing a cache entry. Preserve the SDK response's `status`, `features` and `dateUpdated` fields and the ordinary draft/edit/publish flow. A cache miss should still populate the cache for later reads.
